## Body

STATE at compaction (21 Nov ~04:05 local):
- #298 (F245+F246) R1 = 3 BLOCKs; falcon pushing R2 (FINAL, C34) with 4 items: sweep path repr (lsof escapes, Linux spaces, metadata .ok() drop -> fail closed), bounce-rs /tmp vs /private/tmp alias (dev/ino or realpath), bounded /usr/sbin/lsof in bounce-rs (refuse on timeout), whole sweep read inside 10 s. Prime offered an argv-label liveness option (falcon's call). Seats: reviewer pij-zonal-bee %581, security pij-frequent-sawfish %582, perf snail. Route R2 to the same three.
- F241 APPLY (about 52k dead fixture sockets/locks) is HELD until #298 merges. Then falcon: fresh dry-run -> both counts to prime -> --apply -> final dry-run.
- Bounce pending for #294 (F240) + #295 lock re-check: prime holds it until snail's 4 h RSS reading on daemon 22316 (~05:09 local). RSS reading 1 = 138 MB (settled). F-item only if >200 MB and growing, or >200 at 4 h.
- Seats: falcon (OMP, sole coder; queue empty after #298), snail (performance). Silkworm closed.

LESSONS:
1. Destructive tools: hold the APPLY until a reviewer has proven the liveness input. Each round of #295/#298 found a new way the deciding check was wrong (unlink-under-flock split; Darwin ECONNREFUSED from a LIVE full-backlog listener; lsof escapes; /tmp alias; whitespace parse). Ask the reviewer to reproduce on scratch with real tmux and odd names.
2. A fix that runs at exit/bounce must be proven on the REAL exit path. F238 passed review, but the daemon's HTTP join had no deadline, so bounce SIGKILLed it and the teardown never ran (F242). Ask for a two-bounce live proof: the first may SIGKILL the old daemon, the second must not.
3. Pre-signal helpers in bounce-rs: every probe bounded, absolute path, fail closed (refuse) with PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE=1 override; never synthesize tmux -S (it skips tmux's dir-ownership check: cross-user env leak).
4. C34 final-round new issues: send to prime with a recommendation (usually 'ship with a named F-item folded into the next PR in the same files'). The prime ruled each within minutes.
5. Docs-only follow-up commits (#285, #294): verify with git diff that only comment lines changed, re-freeze, and the verdicts carry.
6. In bash tool calls, put any message holding backticks, angle brackets or $( ) in a file and use --body-file; the tool blocks those patterns inline.
7. Relay snail's baseline-ready before any bounce; the prime holds builds during its windows.
